quizzes.title: Why the MDR framework was introduced
quizzes.passage: Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has grown into a large digital payment infrastructure that handles billions of transactions every month. As the network expands, it serves more users and more transactions, and its server capacity and customer support must keep pace. To meet these needs, the National Payments Corporation of India introduced a Merchant Discount Rate framework for certain UPI transactions. The framework gives the payment ecosystem a revenue mechanism of its own. The zero-MDR policy, introduced in 2020, had exempted merchants from paying any fee for UPI and RuPay transactions to encourage digital adoption, particularly among small traders and informal sectors. The new framework is designed so that everyday low-value transactions remain free, and the government and the payments body have both emphasised protecting small merchants and ordinary users from additional costs. Essential services such as railways, telecom, insurance and fuel are treated separately under the framework. Capital markets also receive a separate treatment. The booklet presents the framework against this background of network growth, and readers should look at its reasons as well as its rates to understand why it was introduced.

questions.q: Under the 'Innovation' reason for the framework, what can its revenue support?
options: Technological improvements and new payment solutions
questions.explanation: The booklet says revenue can support technological improvements and new payment solutions under the Innovation reason.

questions.q: Which reason for the framework is linked to eligible small merchants continuing to receive zero-MDR benefits?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the continued zero-MDR benefit for eligible small merchants under Support for Small Businesses.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The framework was introduced partly to reduce UPI's dependence on continued public funding.
Reason (R): A payment ecosystem with its own revenue mechanism can reduce dependence on continued public funding.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet lists reduced dependence on public funding as a reason, and it says a self-funded ecosystem achieves this.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Financial Sustainability   ->   A. Revenue supports continued operation and expansion
II. Cybersecurity   ->   B. Stronger systems for preventing fraud and cyber threats
III. Innovation   ->   C. Revenue supports technological improvements and new payment solutions
IV. Support for Small Businesses   ->   D. Eligible small merchants keep zero-MDR benefits
questions.explanation: Each reason in List I is paired with its stated description in List II in the booklet.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the reasons for the MDR framework:
I. UPI requires continuous investment in payment infrastructure and technology.
II. MDR revenue is a tax collected by the government.
III. Revenue can support technological improvements and new payment solutions.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The booklet says UPI needs continuous infrastructure investment and that revenue can support new solutions, but MDR is not a government tax.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the MDR framework are correct?
I. Infrastructure development is one of the stated reasons for the framework.
II. MDR revenue is distributed only to the NPCI.
III. Consumer protection is one of the stated reasons for the framework.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet's reasons, while the booklet says MDR is distributed among several participants, not only NPCI.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed among the stated reasons for the framework?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists cybersecurity, innovation and infrastructure development as reasons, but never public-sector advertising.

quizzes.title: Reasons behind the MDR framework
quizzes.passage: The network behind UPI handles a very large number of payments each month, and that volume keeps growing. Growth of this kind places heavy demands on the systems that run the network. Equipment and software must be upgraded regularly, and server capacity must expand as more users join. Customer support also has to be maintained for a large base of users. Fraud and other threats appear as digital payments become more common, so the operators must watch for them constantly. The Merchant Discount Rate framework was introduced to address these demands. It creates a revenue source inside the payment ecosystem. Before the framework, the zero-MDR policy had allowed merchants to accept UPI and RuPay payments without any fee, an arrangement that encouraged digital adoption among small traders and informal sectors. Under the new framework, everyday low-value transactions remain free, and the government and the National Payments Corporation of India have stressed the need to protect small merchants and ordinary users from additional costs. The framework is therefore presented as a way to sustain the network while keeping daily payments affordable for people who use them.

questions.q: Which reason for the framework is linked to revenue supporting technological improvements and new payment solutions? Give one word.
questions.explanation: The booklet names Innovation as the reason that revenue can support technological improvements and new payment solutions.

questions.q: Which reason for the framework is linked to stronger systems against fraud and cyber threats? Give one word.
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Cybersecurity as the reason for stronger systems that prevent fraud and cyber threats.

questions.q: Which reason says that a revenue mechanism can support the continued operation and expansion of UPI? Give two words.
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Financial Sustainability as the reason about revenue supporting UPI's continued operation and expansion.

questions.q: The framework is meant to reduce dependence on continued ____ funding. Give one word.
questions.explanation: The booklet says a self-funded ecosystem can reduce dependence on continued public funding.

questions.q: Which reason is linked to continuous investment in payment infrastructure and technology? Give two words.
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Infrastructure Development as the reason that UPI needs continuous investment in payment infrastructure and technology.

questions.q: Which reason for the framework is named after the protection it gives to people? Give two words.
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Consumer Protection as the reason that the framework keeps P2P and low-value merchant payments free.

questions.q: Which reason's name begins with 'Support for' and concerns eligible small merchants? Give the two words that follow 'Support for'.
questions.explanation: The booklet's reason is titled Support for Small Businesses, and eligible small merchants continue to receive zero-MDR benefits under it.

quizzes.title: MDR, UPI and NPCI basics
quizzes.passage: Unified Payments Interface, widely known as UPI, lets people send and receive money through mobile applications linked to their bank accounts. Individuals use it to pay one another, and merchants use it to accept payments at shops, restaurants and online outlets. The network has grown into a major platform that handles a very large number of transactions every month, and its services are meant for both small and large users. Many everyday low-value transactions take place on it. Behind the system is an organisation that operates and develops retail payment and settlement systems in India. Digital payments have expanded over the years, and the booklet links this growth to the need for continued investment. Keeping such a network working smoothly is a continuing task, and the booklet describes several areas that need attention as it grows. The framework discussed in the booklet applies to merchant payments above a certain value and treats some sectors separately. Readers who want to understand it should look at its slabs, its exemptions and the reasons behind it.

questions.q: Among which participants is the MDR distributed, according to the booklet?
options: Banks, payment service providers and other relevant participants
questions.explanation: The booklet says MDR is distributed among banks, payment service providers and other relevant participants in the payment ecosystem.

questions.q: Which of the following is a stated feature of UPI?
options: Available only during bank working hours
Limited to transactions within one bank
questions.explanation: The booklet describes UPI as a real-time, 24/7, instant and interoperable payment system.

questions.q: Which of the following countries is NOT listed in the booklet as accepting UPI?
questions.explanation: Italy does not appear in the booklet's list of countries that accept UPI, which includes Nepal, Qatar and Mauritius.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): UPI is accepted in several countries outside India.
Reason (R): UPI is a real-time, 24/7, instant and interoperable payment system.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true in the booklet, but the system's real-time features do not explain its acceptance in other countries.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. MDR   ->   A. Fee for processing a digital payment, borne by the merchant
II. UPI   ->   B. Real-time, 24/7 interoperable payment system
III. NPCI   ->   C. Umbrella organisation for retail payment and settlement systems
IV. MDR revenue   ->   D. Remains within the payment ecosystem
questions.explanation: Each term in List I is matched with its description in List II as given in the booklet.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the payment system in the booklet:
I. MDR is a tax collected by the government.
II. Sri Lanka is among the countries that accept UPI.
III. Qatar is among the countries that accept UPI.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements II and III match the booklet's country list, while the booklet explicitly says MDR is not a tax.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. MDR is a fee charged for processing a digital payment transaction.
II. UPI was developed by the Reserve Bank of India.
III. Mauritius is a country listed among those accepting UPI.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are in the booklet, while the booklet says UPI was developed by NPCI, not by the RBI.

quizzes.title: UPI, MDR and NPCI terms
quizzes.passage: UPI is used for transfers between individuals and for payments made to merchants. The payments are made through mobile applications, and the network processes them quickly. One category of payments is made from a customer to a business, and the booklet explains how fees apply to such payments. The fee charged for handling a digital payment is known by a short form that appears throughout the booklet. The fee falls on the business that receives the money, while the framework for it is designed around a few value slabs. The revenue from these fees stays within the network and helps support its work. Among the countries listed as accepting the system are several in Asia, along with a small number of other nations on different continents. The network is operated by a body whose functions include developing and operating payment systems across the country. Many small businesses and informal sectors were encouraged to adopt digital payments in earlier years, when merchants paid no fee at all. The booklet presents the framework as one that fits into the wider payment ecosystem and protects ordinary users from additional costs. Readers who want to understand the framework should look at its slabs, its exemptions and the reasons behind it.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation MDR stand for? Give the full name.
questions.explanation: The booklet uses MDR as the short form for Merchant Discount Rate, the fee charged for processing digital payments.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation UPI stand for? Give the full name.
questions.explanation: The booklet introduces UPI as the Unified Payments Interface.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation P2M stand for? Give the phrase with hyphens between the words.
questions.explanation: The booklet refers to P2M UPI transactions as Person-to-Merchant transactions.

questions.q: Which Middle East nation in the booklet's list of UPI-accepting countries is named by its abbreviation? Give the abbreviation.
questions.explanation: The booklet lists UAE as the Middle East nation among the countries that accept UPI.

questions.q: Which European nation, other than Greece, is listed as accepting UPI? Give the country name.
questions.explanation: The booklet lists France as the first European nation to accept UPI, alongside Greece.

questions.q: The booklet describes UPI as a system that works across different banks and platforms. Which single word describes this quality?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes UPI as an instant, interoperable payment system.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation NPCI stand for? Give the full name.
questions.explanation: The booklet expands NPCI as the National Payments Corporation of India.
